overview: The Medford Zoning Board of Appeals is the municipal body responsible for adjudicating petitions for variances, special permits, and administrative appeals under local zoning bylaws and Massachusetts General Laws, including Chapter 40B comprehensive permits. Over the course of 31 meetings spanning from February 2024 to September 2026, the board reviewed major comprehensive residential developments, evaluated commercial and residential relief requests, and addressed administrative appeals. Its proceedings regularly involved peer reviews for traffic, architecture, and civil engineering, alongside assessments of neighborhood impacts, off-street parking, and nonconforming structures. Most recently, the board has been deliberating on residential additions and multi-family conversions while reviewing new state regulations governing accessory dwelling units.

threads.name: 970 Fellsway Chapter 40B development
threads.summary: Beginning in early 2024, the board engaged in multi-session comprehensive permit hearings for a 289-unit residential project at 970 Fellsway, directing the applicant to refine conceptual plans to include building height reductions, step-downs near neighbors, and green space improvements. Across subsequent meetings, members and peer reviewers assessed detailed architectural massing, traffic impact analyses, civil site circulation, and underground stormwater management systems. In May 2024, the board determined that market-rate units in the development were subject to Medford's linkage ordinance and voted to approve the Chapter 40B comprehensive permit with a partial linkage fee waiver of $816,564.24 based on off-site public improvements. Later, in January 2025, the board granted a special permit to allow partial demolition of a commercial building on the site to facilitate an associated lot split.

threads.name: Mystic Avenue development proposals
threads.summary: The board resumed review of a Chapter 40B comprehensive permit application for an eight-story, 378-unit residential project at 280 Mystic Avenue, authorizing peer review consultants for architecture, civil engineering, and traffic. By late May 2024, the board found the applicant had been unresponsive and imposed a deadline for required peer review fees. At the June 2024 meeting, the board voted to accept the applicant's formal request to withdraw the 378-unit Chapter 40B comprehensive permit petition. Separately, at 400 Mystic Avenue, the board approved an amendment to a prior height variance allowing the construction of a 50.5-foot auto dealership service facility and car elevator.

threads.name: Cannabis dispensary permitting at 114 Mystic Avenue
threads.summary: In May 2026, the board considered special permit requests for Victory Gardens at 114 Mystic Avenue, voting to approve permits for medical cannabis sales and product manufacturing while continuing an application for courier delivery services to seek input from the police chief. The delivery permit hearing was continued again in June 2026 pending legal counsel. In July 2026, the board officially voted to approve the special permit allowing courier delivery services at the facility.

threads.name: Accessory Dwelling Unit petitions on Vassar and Wellesley Streets
threads.summary: In July 2026, the board took up companion applications for 1-3 Vassar Street and 12 Wellesley Street seeking variances to expand attic spaces and construct dormers for accessory dwelling units, continuing both to consult city legal counsel regarding new state zoning regulations. Both cases were continued again in August 2026 at the request of the petitioner's counsel to allow voting members to review prior session recordings. In September 2026, the board voted to continue both matters to October 29, 2026, allowing the applicant to submit reduced architectural designs and giving the board time to seek further legal counsel on state regulations.

threads.name: Two-family conversions and multi-family residential relief
threads.summary: The board routinely adjudicated applications seeking use and dimensional variances or special permits to construct or convert properties into two-family or multi-family dwellings. While some requests were denied due to a lack of demonstrated statutory hardship, such as at 65 Burgett Avenue and 52 Garfield Avenue, others were approved, including conversions on Pearl Street, Morton Avenue, Marion Street, and Main Street. At 85 Elm Street, the board evaluated use and dimensional variances to replace a motor vehicle repair shop with a three-unit townhouse, continuing the case across several sessions before granting approval in February 2025. Across 2025 and 2026, the board granted further approvals for residential conversions on Second Street, Main Street, and Surrey Street.

threads.name: Administrative operations, rules, and leadership
threads.summary: The board underwent several leadership changes, electing Jamie Thompson as chair in April 2024 following the resignation of Mike Caldera, who continued to act as chair specifically for the 970 Fellsway proceedings to maintain consistency. In February 2025, following Thompson's resignation, the board re-elected Mike Caldera as chair. Administratively, the board addressed delayed meeting minutes throughout 2024 and 2025, exploring transcription tools and AI software to clear backlogs, and considered recommendations from the Building Commissioner to appoint a subcommittee to revise its rules and regulations.

periods.narrative: During this term, the board focused extensively on large-scale Chapter 40B developments, successfully approving the 970 Fellsway project and resolving petitions on Mystic Avenue while addressing numerous residential variance and special permit applications.
This term centered on commercial and cannabis special permits, residential additions, administrative enforcement appeals, and the ongoing interpretation of state accessory dwelling unit regulations.
